items.headline: Tamber music creation suite gets a 2.0 update: here's everything you need to know
items.excerpt: The "ethically trained" AI music creation suite Tamber has shipped v2.0, splitting its five core tools — Gestures, Tamby, Librarian, City Packs and Sonic Atlas — into connected apps. Gestures now runs as a VST3/AU plugin with new synth and vocoder engines and lower latency, while the Tamby in-session co-producer becomes a summonable overlay with chat history.

items.headline: Guilt-Free AI: These 6 AI music tools actually pay the artists behind them
items.excerpt: A round-up of AI music tools that license their training data and share revenue with contributing artists, including LANDR, Moises AI, Voice-Swap and Neutone. Voice-Swap and Neutone both pay 50% back to the singers and model-makers involved.

items.headline: NOMZ Studios Updates StemMaster to v1.1.35 — Optional AI Engine Now Runs Locally
items.excerpt: StemMaster, the Windows app that mixes and masters a full multitrack from its individual stems, moves its optional AI engine on-device so sessions no longer have to leave the machine. It's the 34th release since launch.

items.headline: Hotone Pulze Jr. — the mini amp with AI onboard
items.excerpt: Hotone's pocket-sized modelling amp puts onboard AI tone-shaping into a practice-rig form factor, pushing neural amp modelling out of the plugin window and into cheap portable hardware.

items.headline: AI Music Charts 2026: Australia bans AI-generated songs, joining a growing global trend
items.excerpt: ARIA now excludes wholly or mostly AI-generated songs from Australia's official charts, with AI-assisted records still eligible if they are substantially human-made. More than 20 chart programmes worldwide have adopted comparable rules.

items.headline: Musicians & Actors Unite in Campaign Against Voice Cloning for AI
items.excerpt: A coalition of UK musicians and actors has written to the government demanding stronger protection against unauthorised cloning of their voices, targeting the consent rules that govern singing-voice models.

items.headline: Epidemic Sound Offers a Strikingly Different Licensing Approach
items.excerpt: Epidemic Sound is pitching pre-cleared catalogue as the safe alternative for brands and creators scoring social video, as AI-generated soundtracks and takedown risk push creative teams toward fully licensed music.

items.headline: Free, Open Source StemDeck Stem Separator For Linux, Mac & Windows
items.excerpt: StemDeck is a free, open-source stem extraction platform that isolates vocals, drums, bass, piano and guitar for practice, transcription, remixing and creative audio work — locally, on all three desktop platforms.

items.headline: AI models can identify iconic jazz pianists from their recordings — and reveal their "musical fingerprints"
items.excerpt: New research shows models can attribute performances to individual jazz pianists and surface the micro-timing and voicing habits that define them. The authors suggest it could be used to propose authors for unattributed recordings.

items.headline: 'Human-First' Needs More Than Just a Checkbox
items.excerpt: Anti-AI and human-made labels currently rest on self-attestation, which the piece argues cannot survive contact with the real world. It proposes an independently administered certification system for human-made music.

items.headline: Mark My Words: AI Music Is the End of the Artist Economy
items.excerpt: An argument against treating generative music as "inevitable": if making a song no longer requires an artist, the piece contends, what collapses is not craft but the economy that pays for it.

items.headline: Instagram First Draft Auto-Edits Reels In Seconds
items.excerpt: Instagram's free First Draft feature automatically trims clips and removes awkward pauses to assemble a Reel, handing musicians a zero-effort first cut for the video work that now sits between a release and its audience.

items.headline: Trama is a FREE offline AI stem separator for Windows, macOS, and Linux
items.excerpt: Ohlhorst Digital's Trama splits mixed tracks into vocals, drums, bass and other entirely offline — no account, no cloud upload, no separate model download. Normal/High/Ultra presets trade time for extra separation passes, with batch queuing built in.

items.headline: Chinese Tech Giant Alibaba Launches New AI Music Generator Called 'Happy Shrimp'
items.excerpt: Alibaba's HappyShrimp 1.0 beta generates fully produced songs from prompts that can specify instrumentation, vocal style and how a track's energy shifts over time. Chinese major Taihe Music Group is signed up for artist co-creation.

items.headline: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music
items.excerpt: Billboard says it will identify songs on its charts and in its editorial coverage that use AI, leaning on creator disclosure plus detection tools such as Luminate's AI identification programme.

items.headline: University of Alberta Study Finds 87% of Canadian Musicians View Generative AI 'Negatively'
items.excerpt: A survey of 263 Canadian musicians found overwhelmingly negative attitudes toward generative AI, alongside their views on streaming platforms as an artistic tool.

items.headline: Cyanite rolls out a big upgrade to its AI music-tagging tech
items.excerpt: German startup Cyanite, an early mover in AI music metadata, has shipped a major upgrade to its auto-tagging engine — the layer that decides how sync teams and catalogues actually find a track.
